- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to offset momentum.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to account for mean reversion or risk aversion.
- Model shows persistent lag in low-price zones (e.g., <70.0); if sentiment is neutral or negative, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment shifts sharply within 5 days, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect new sentiment direction.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
